verdict.rationale: GitHub Projects is built directly on the repository's issues and pull requests, so it tracks the same items rather than copies of them. The docs state that changing an assignee in the project shows up in the issue, and that dragging issues between assignee groups changes issue assignment. missing for 10: explicit documentation of the issue-to-project direction beyond the assignee example, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an engineer, I can keep tasks bi-directionally synced with my code repository's issue tracker instead of duplicating data

citations.quote: For example, change an assignee in your project and that change is shown in your issue.
group your project by assignee, and make changes to issue assignment by dragging issues into the different groups.
You can use custom fields to add metadata to your issues, pull requests, and draft issues
Turn ideas into Issues and track them with Projects.
